title: What do recent papers say about memory for long-running coding agents?

turns.question: What do recent papers say about memory for long-running coding agents?

answer.text: Replay buffers are the strongest result for long-running coding agents: replaying exact tool results and dropping the ones that stop mattering cut tokens per task by 41% on 40 long-horizon tasks [S1].

citations.title: Replay Buffers Beat Summaries for Long-Running Coding Agents

answer.text: The authors compare against a summary-based baseline on 40 long-horizon coding tasks and report tokens per task and retries, with no loss in task success [S1]. Every task is Python, so the result is a reason to test the idea on your own harness, not to adopt it [S1].

citations.title: Replay Buffers Beat Summaries for Long-Running Coding Agents

answer.text: The benchmark is small and every task is Python, so the gain is measured on one language and one harness shape [S1]. The paper does not report a run over several days, which is where a replay buffer's storage cost would matter most [S1].

citations.title: Replay Buffers Beat Summaries for Long-Running Coding Agents
